title: 29-layer HfO2/MgF2 UV bandpass filter with damped thickness optimization
scientific_hypothesis: A 29-layer alternating HfO2/MgF2 stack with individually tunable thicknesses can produce a transmission passband at 255-280 nm while maintaining suppression at 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm, and reducing the thickness perturbation envelope will stabilize convergence without sacrificing final performance.
design_principle: Recalled thin-film interference physics: alternating high-index (HfO2) and low-index (MgF2) layers create distributed Bragg reflector stopbands. Passbands emerge from deliberate thickness deviations from quarter-wave condition at the target wavelength. The perturbation envelope controls how far each layer can deviate from its starting thickness during optimization.
proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | fused silica substrate (29 film layers total, alternating starting with HfO2)
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 29 layers
thickness perturbation envelope reduced to ±2.5 nm from prior ±5.0 nm
soft_objectives: maintain physically valid candidates throughout optimization
manufacturing_considerations: HfO2 and MgF2 are conventional evaporatable/sputterable dielectrics
individual layer thicknesses should remain in manufacturable range 30-200 nm
theory_basis: Recalled: Quarter-wave stacks produce stopbands centered at design wavelength with bandwidth proportional to index contrast
Recalled: HfO2 has higher refractive index than MgF2 in UV-visible range, creating useful index contrast for interference filters
Recalled: Passbands in Bragg mirrors can be created by introducing thickness defects or varying layer thicknesses away from quarter-wave condition
Recalled: Smaller optimization perturbation envelopes reduce oscillatory behavior in gradient-based thickness optimization
Recalled: L-BFGS quasi-Newton methods converge more smoothly than simple gradient descent for smooth objective functions like thin-film transmission spectra
expected_advantages: Reduced perturbation envelope (±2.5 nm) should suppress high-frequency thickness oscillations seen in prior iterations
L-BFGS optimizer should provide more stable convergence than previous gradient_thickness routine
Maintaining 29-layer topology preserves comparability across all prior iterations of this control route
Alternating HfO2/MgF2 provides maximum index contrast from available dielectric materials in catalog
known_risks: Uncertain whether HfO2 extinction coefficient remains low enough at 255 nm - would need to verify measured k values in material registry
Uncertain whether 29 layers is optimal count vs. fewer layers with different topology - this route does not test layer count variation
Uncertain whether MgF2 maintains sufficient transparency at 255 nm - some fluoride materials show absorption edges in deep UV
The ±2.5 nm envelope may be too restrictive if prior iterations were stuck in local minima requiring larger moves to escape
No literature verification of HfO2/MgF2 compatibility for solar-blind UV filters - this is recalled design practice only
execution_request_english: Optimize a 29-layer planar multilayer thin-film stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2 (29 film layers total). Optimize all 29 individual layer thicknesses using L-BFGS quasi-Newton optimizer for 150 fixed iterations. Thickness perturbation bounds: ±2.5 nm from current best candidate thicknesses. Spectral targets: maximize transmittance 255-280 nm, minimize transmittance 300-700 nm, minimize transmittance 700-1100 nm. No metal layers. Materials: hfo2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), SiO2 (Gao) substrate. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, thicknesses_nm for each round.
revision_reason: Continuation of control route with damped optimization: reduced thickness perturbation envelope from ±5.0 nm to ±2.5 nm and switched to L-BFGS quasi-Newton optimizer for 150 iterations to suppress high-frequency oscillations while preserving the 29-layer HfO2/MgF2 alternating topology from prior iterations.
